summary: Round 04 (semantics-first, manuscript read directly). Verdicts: round 03's Z-time digraph reading and limit-closure results are faithful to the manuscript (which states limit closure itself as upward-directed gluing resting on Saturation), but round 03 wrongly cast stab as Ockhamist historical necessity: the manuscript's past-sharing modality is its open-future operator, and the Ockhamist axiom HN fails for stab (compiled) while holding for the open-future operator (compiled). Compiled at every temporal order, no frame axiom: stab truth is a function of the present state; a state-naming rule is sound frame by frame; truth is preserved by the clock projection, whose histories never revisit a state; Limit holds in the clock product given Nullity; truth is invariant under order-automorphic re-timing of histories (L+ sees no durations). Paper: all-histories semantics equals bundled semantics over topologically closed bundles; the canonical-frame obligation is that every trace in the closure of the canonical bundle is coherent; finite-colour engines face no frame-axiom obstacle at any class. Manuscript inventory: no live proof system or completeness claim for stab; its commented-out TM+ equals PlusAxiom's stability block (plus stab_4); its commented-out remark that TM+ completeness over all task frames remains open is answered negatively by reports 01-02. No completeness theorem stated. 560 rescope (plus_incomplete_base with BLC) unchanged.
